sources.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333 Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 20
sources.locator: Complete 15-page lecture PDF; photon-gas section, equations VI.49–VI.61 (PDF pp. 12–14; printed pp. 128–131): periodic wavevectors, two polarizations, oscillator occupation, partition product, Planck energy density, continuum limit, c/4 angular flux, and spectral law.
sources.reading_extent: The complete photon-gas section and surrounding discussion were read from the full PDF. The separate phonon treatment is not used as a supplier. The source's continuum sum-to-integral step is treated as motivation; the local Riemann-sum proof supplies the required convergence.

contents.name: Equations VI.49–VI.53: two-polarization periodic modes, oscillator occupations, and partition product

source_review.read_extent: Read the photon-mode setup, the two transverse polarization labels, periodic wavevectors, the zero-point convention, and the product over occupation states in the complete photon section.
source_review.supports: The conventional mode energies, two-polarization multiplicity, geometric occupation factor, and product-trace formula used for comparison with the explicit local model.
source_review.limitations: The notes do not prove trace-class convergence for the countably infinite finite-box mode set or treat the zero mode as a separate trace obstruction. Those arguments are supplied locally, with the zero mode excluded from the theorem's model.

contents.name: Equations VI.51–VI.52 and VI.60–VI.61: continuum Planck energy density and spectral dependence

source_review.read_extent: Read the dimensionless substitution, the integral for total excitation energy, the wavevector spectrum, and the stated frequency dependence.
source_review.supports: The standard Planck energy density and T-to-the-fourth integrated energy formula against which the local exact Riemann limit is checked.
source_review.limitations: The source uses the continuum mode-density approximation and does not prove the uniform small-momentum, large-momentum, or singular-entropy estimates required here.

contents.name: Equations VI.52 and VI.54: dimensionless Planck energy and logarithmic free-energy integrals

source_review.read_extent: Read the dimensionless excitation-energy integral and the logarithmic oscillator contribution to the free energy in the complete photon section.
source_review.supports: The standard values of the two dimensionless integrals after continuum mode counting.
source_review.limitations: The lecture does not derive these values from the Fourier theorem used here. The local proof derives zeta(4) from Parseval and applies monotone convergence to the positive series.

contents.name: Equations VI.56–VI.59: isotropic one-sided angular energy flux

source_review.read_extent: Read the hemisphere integral for the velocity component normal to an opening and its c/4 factor.
source_review.supports: The angular factor converting an isotropic energy density into one-sided flux and the Stefan coefficient after the Planck energy integral.
source_review.limitations: The local result states an explicit ideal isotropic ray-transport model and does not identify it with an observed emitter, a horizon process, or a greybody calculation.

contents.name: Standard Planck flux input to the separately defined effective-area mass ODE

source_review.read_extent: The c/4 angular flux and Stefan coefficient were read in the same photon section.
source_review.supports: Only the Planck-flux formula reused from the A-page theorem.
source_review.limitations: The source supplies none of the local mass ODE, area proportionality, fixed asymptotic normalization, cutoff, or entropy-accounting assumptions; these are stated and proved conditionally in the proposition.

sources.title: University of Mississippi PHY 727 course notes, Lecture 18: The Photon Gas
sources.locator: Complete two-page lecture note: pp. 1–2, mode and Fock occupations, partition function, continuum density of states, free energy, entropy, energy density, and Planck spectrum.
sources.reading_extent: Both pages of the complete two-page PDF were inspected, including the explicit qualifications about how equilibrium is established and the use of a continuum density-of-states approximation.

short_document_reading.publication: University of Mississippi PHY 727, Lecture 18, The Photon Gas; complete two-page lecture note.
short_document_reading.completeness_evidence: The full PDF bytes were retrieved and both PDF pages were inspected in the rendered full-text view; the source itself identifies the complete lecture as pages 1–2.

contents.name: Pages 1–2: occupation states, product partition trace, and two polarizations

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete finite-box mode, occupation, Hamiltonian, and partition-function account on both pages.
source_review.supports: The conventional massless mode spectrum, two-polarization multiplicity, zero-chemical-potential Bose occupation, and factorized formal partition product.
source_review.limitations: The source presents the product formally and does not establish convergence of the infinite trace. The local argument supplies the shell estimate and invokes the exact QSM diagonal-trace interface conditionally.

contents.name: Pages 1–2: density of states, Planck spectrum, energy, free energy, and entropy density

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete continuum density-of-states calculation, Planck spectral expression, zeta-four integral, and entropy/energy relations.
source_review.supports: An independent treatment of the continuum Planck spectrum, Stefan energy density, and radiation entropy density.
source_review.limitations: Its entropy is obtained from a thermodynamic-potential derivative after a continuum approximation; it does not prove the exact entropy of the full finite-box diagonal Gibbs state. The local proof establishes that entropy directly from its eigenvalue sum and proves the singular Riemann limit.

contents.name: Pages 1–2: zeta-four energy integral and logarithmic free-energy integral

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete free-energy dimensionless integral, the integration-by-parts reduction, and the displayed value zeta(4)=pi^4/90.
source_review.supports: The standard values of the positive energy and logarithmic integrals used in the Planck constants.
source_review.limitations: The note uses the continuum density-of-states calculation. The assigned local lemma supplies a separate Parseval proof and uses monotone convergence to justify the integral-series identities.

contents.name: Planck energy input to the separately defined effective-area mass ODE

source_review.read_extent: The continuum Planck energy and entropy expressions were read on page 2.
source_review.supports: Only the Planck flux input reused from the A-page theorem.
source_review.limitations: The course notes do not supply the proposition's effective area, asymptotic reference, mass evolution law, or cutoff; each remains an explicit mathematical model premise.
